# CFA MULTITRAIT MULTIMETHOD



::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

:::




## Data simulation
Data are simulated using lavaan from a three-factor model (t1 t2 t3). The rows are then split into three arbitrary blocks labelled m1 m2 m3 and reshaped to wide format. Because each block comes from different simulated cases, the data contain no method variance and no shared trait variance across methods. They only illustrate how to specify and compare the models; they cannot show convergent or discriminant validity.



::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
# specify population model
population_model<-'t1=~x1+0.8*x2+1.2*x3
                   t2=~x4+0.5*x5+1.5*x6
                   t3=~x7+0.1*x8+0.9*x9'
# generate data
set.seed(1234)
model_data<-lavaan::simulateData(population_model,sample.nobs=45000)
model_data$method<-c(rep("m1",15000),rep("m2",15000),rep("m3",15000))
model_data$id<-rep(1:15000,3)[1:45000]
mtmm_data<-reshape(model_data,idvar="id",timevar="method",direction="wide")
```
:::




## Parameter estimation and model inspection for the simulated data



::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
default_model<-'t1=~x1+x2+x3
                t2=~x4+x5+x6
                t3=~x7+x8+x9'
dm<-lavaan::cfa(default_model,data=model_data)
findex<-c("rmsea","cfi","tli","rni","rfi","ifi","srmr","gfi")
# lavaan::inspect(dm,what="std")
# lavaan::parameterEstimates(dm,standardized=TRUE)
lavaan::fitMeasures(dm,findex)
```

## Model specification for MTMM
Following Widaman (1985) and Byrne (2016, ch. 10), CFA MTMM requires at least four nested models
- Model 1 Freely correlated traits and methods  
- Model 2 No traits – freely correlated methods  
- Model 3 Perfectly correlated traits – freely correlated methods  
- Model 4 Freely correlated traits – perfectly independent methods  

Then models 2-4 are compared with model 1
- Model 2 should be worse than model 1 (convergent validity)
- Model 3 should be worse than model 1 (discriminant validity among traits)
- Model 4 should be as good as model 1 (discriminant validity among methods, no common method bias)

It is easier to specify these models incrementally.



::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
methods<-"
method_1=~x1.m1+x2.m1+x3.m1+x4.m1+x5.m1+x6.m1+x7.m1+x8.m1+x9.m1
method_2=~x1.m2+x2.m2+x3.m2+x4.m2+x5.m2+x6.m2+x7.m2+x8.m2+x9.m2
method_3=~x1.m3+x2.m3+x3.m3+x4.m3+x5.m3+x6.m3+x7.m3+x8.m3+x9.m3
"
traits<-" 
t1=~x1.m1+x2.m1+x3.m1+x1.m2+x2.m2+x3.m2+x1.m3+x2.m3+x3.m3
t2=~x4.m1+x5.m1+x6.m1+x4.m2+x5.m2+x6.m2+x4.m3+x5.m3+x6.m3
t3=~x7.m1+x8.m1+x9.m1+x7.m2+x8.m2+x9.m2+x7.m3+x8.m3+x9.m3
"
covariances<-"
method_1~~0*t1
method_1~~0*t2
method_1~~0*t3
method_2~~0*t1
method_2~~0*t2
method_2~~0*t3
method_3~~0*t1
method_3~~0*t2
method_3~~0*t3
"
perfectly_correlated_traits<-"
t1~~1*t2
t1~~1*t3
t2~~1*t3
"
perfectly_correlated_methods<-"
method_1~~1*method_2
method_1~~1*method_3
method_2~~1*method_3
"
perfectly_independent_methods<-"
method_1~~0*method_2
method_1~~0*method_3
method_2~~0*method_3
"
correlated_residuals<-"
x1.m1~~x1.m2
x1.m1~~x1.m3
x1.m2~~x1.m3
x2.m1~~x2.m2
x2.m1~~x2.m3
x2.m2~~x2.m3
x3.m1~~x3.m2
x3.m1~~x3.m3
x3.m2~~x3.m3
x4.m1~~x4.m2
x4.m1~~x4.m3
x4.m2~~x4.m3
x5.m1~~x5.m2
x5.m1~~x5.m3
x5.m2~~x5.m3
x6.m1~~x6.m2
x6.m1~~x6.m3
x6.m2~~x6.m3
x7.m1~~x7.m2
x7.m1~~x7.m3
x7.m2~~x7.m3
x8.m1~~x8.m2
x8.m1~~x8.m3
x8.m2~~x8.m3
x9.m1~~x9.m2
x9.m1~~x9.m3
x9.m2~~x9.m3
"

perfectly_correlated_residuals<-"
x1.m1~~1*x1.m2
x1.m2~~1*x1.m3
x2.m1~~1*x2.m2
x2.m2~~1*x2.m3
x3.m1~~1*x3.m2
x3.m2~~1*x3.m3
x4.m1~~1*x4.m2
x4.m2~~1*x4.m3
x5.m1~~1*x5.m2
x5.m2~~1*x5.m3
x6.m1~~1*x6.m2
x6.m2~~1*x6.m3
x7.m1~~1*x7.m2
x7.m2~~1*x7.m3
x8.m1~~1*x8.m2
x8.m2~~1*x8.m3
x9.m1~~1*x9.m2
x9.m2~~1*x9.m3
"

freely_correlated_traits_methods_model<-paste0(traits,methods,covariances)
methods_only_model<-methods
perfectly_correlated_traits_model<-paste0(freely_correlated_traits_methods_model,perfectly_correlated_traits)
perfectly_correlated_methods_model<-paste0(freely_correlated_traits_methods_model,perfectly_correlated_methods)
perfectly_independent_methods_model<-paste0(freely_correlated_traits_methods_model,perfectly_independent_methods)
correlated_residuals_model<-paste0(traits,correlated_residuals)
perfectly_correlated_residuals_model<-paste0(traits,perfectly_correlated_residuals)
```
:::

## Model 1 Freely correlated traits and methods

```{.r .cell-code}
fm<-lavaan::cfa(freely_correlated_traits_methods_model,data=mtmm_data,std.lv=TRUE)

# lavaan::fitMeasures(fm,findex)
semPlot::semPaths(fm,"model",whatLabels="std",layout="tree2",residuals=FALSE,exoCov=TRUE,bifactor=c("t1","t2","t3"),rotation=2,sizeLat=2,sizeMan=2)
```

## Comparisons



::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Compare 
# freely correlated traits / freely correlated methods
# no traits / freely correlated methods
lavaan::anova(fm,mm) # Evidence of convergent validity for significant results
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

Chi-Squared Difference Test

    Df     AIC     BIC Chisq Chisq diff RMSEA Df diff          Pr(>Chisq)    
fm 291 1344078 1344741 16824                                                 
mm 321 1365186 1365620 37991      21168 0.217      30 <0.0000000000000002 ***
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
# Compare
# freely correlated traits / freely correlated methods
# perfectly correlated traits / freely correlated methods
lavaan::anova(fm,ctm) # Evidence of discriminant validity among traits for significant results (a lenient test, since traits are only tested against r = 1)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

Chi-Squared Difference Test

     Df     AIC     BIC Chisq Chisq diff RMSEA Df diff          Pr(>Chisq)    
fm  291 1344078 1344741 16824                                                 
ctm 294 1356623 1357263 29374      12550 0.528       3 <0.0000000000000002 ***
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
# Compare
# freely correlated traits / freely correlated methods
# freely correlated traits / perfectly independent methods
lavaan::anova(fm,imm) # Evidence of discriminant validity among methods (no common method bias) for non significant results
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

Chi-Squared Difference Test

     Df     AIC     BIC Chisq Chisq diff RMSEA Df diff          Pr(>Chisq)    
fm  291 1344078 1344741 16824                                                 
imm 294 1352882 1353522 25633       8810 0.442       3 <0.0000000000000002 ***
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
```


:::
:::




Note: with these simulated data the freely correlated traits and methods model fits poorly (CFI = 0.76), and Model 4 gives an improper solution (smallest estimated residual variance = -0.84). The chi-square differences therefore reflect misspecification, not real convergent or discriminant validity. Check fit and admissibility of every model before interpreting the comparisons.

# Other models

## Freely correlated traits – perfectly correlated methods 



::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
cmm<-lavaan::cfa(perfectly_correlated_methods_model,data=mtmm_data,std.lv=TRUE)
# lavaan::inspect(cmm,what="std")
# lavaan::parameterEstimates(cmm,standardized=TRUE)
# lavaan::fitMeasures(cmm,findex)
semPlot::semPaths(cmm,"model",whatLabels="std",layout="tree2",residuals=FALSE,exoCov=TRUE,bifactor=c("t1","t2","t3"),rotation=2,sizeLat=2,sizeMan=2)
```

## Freely correlated traits – indicator-specific correlated residuals
Residuals of the same indicator are correlated across methods (e.g. x1.m1 with x1.m2). This models indicator-specific effects. It is not the correlated-uniqueness MTMM model (Kenny, 1976; Marsh, 1989), which correlates residuals of indicators sharing the same method.



::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
crm<-lavaan::cfa(correlated_residuals_model,data=mtmm_data,std.lv=TRUE)
# lavaan::inspect(crm,what="std")
# lavaan::parameterEstimates(crm,standardized=TRUE)
# lavaan::fitMeasures(crm,findex)
semPlot::semPaths(crm,"model",whatLabels="std",layout="spring",residuals=FALSE,exoCov=TRUE,rotation=2,sizeLat=2.5,sizeMan=2.5)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](EXAMPLE_MULTITRAIT_MULTIMETHOD_files/figure-html/m7-1.png){fig-align='center' width=4500}
